title: CMOS Processing Technology
intro: How CMOS wafers become transistors, resistors, capacitors and wires, and which process facts constrain analog design and layout (Razavi, Chapter 18).

blocks.text: The process in four kinds of step

items: Wafer processing: a high-quality single-crystal substrate with the right doping.
Lithography: transfers each layout layer (well, active, poly, implants, contacts, metals) to the wafer with a mask.
Adding material: oxidation, deposition and ion implantation.
Removing material: etching. Many steps also need a furnace (heat treatment).

blocks.text: A modern process runs over 200 steps and about 30 masks, but the structures it builds are the familiar ones: n-wells, active areas, gate oxide and polysilicon, implanted sources and drains with well and substrate ties, and a stack of metal layers.

blocks.alt: Cross-section with a p-substrate. On the left an NMOS with n+ source and drain and a poly gate, plus a p+ substrate tie; on the right an n-well containing a PMOS with p+ source and drain and an n+ well tie. Shallow trench oxide separates the regions.
blocks.caption: A finished NMOS/PMOS pair with substrate and well ties.

items: Basic Fabrication Steps: sheet resistance, wafers, lithography, oxidation, implantation, deposition and etching.
Transistor Fabrication: the front-end sequence, self-alignment, silicide, contacts and metal.
Passive Devices: resistors and capacitors in CMOS and their imperfections.
Interconnects and Latch-Up: wire resistance and capacitance, electromigration, and the parasitic thyristor.

blocks.text: Why an analog designer cares: process steps explain matching (implant tilt, gradients), parasitics (junction, overlap and wire capacitance), the limits of passive components, and latch-up rules in the layout.

blocks.title: Mask budget
blocks.text: A process has a front end needing 5 masks and 6 metal layers. How many masks does the back end need if each metal layer needs one mask for its contacts or vias and one for the metal, plus one passivation mask?
solution: Back end: $6 \times 2 + 1 = 13$; total about 18. Masks are expensive and each costs a slow lithography sequence, which is why mask count drives cost.
